programmes.d: Two armed bank robbers hit a Seattle bank taking over 150,000 dollars. Before they can escape police confront them and the pair splits up. As authorities search block by block they learn one was a career criminal with a long history of violence.
The body of an unidentified young woman turned up on a highway in a small Pennsylvania town.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Melissa Brannen: Missing
programmes.d: In 1989, residents of a close-knit apartment community in Virginia gathered for a holiday celebration. For Tammy Brannen and five-year-old daughter Melissa, Christmas was always a special time. Then, without warning, the little girl was gone.
The bodies of several young women began turning up in shallow graves in the Alaskan wilderness.

A Chicago street gang thought they had figured out how to kidnap people for ransom again and again, and never get caught. But their one mistake was they underestimated the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
A corrupt local government hinders the investigation of a double murder.
In Langley, Virginia, a terrorist fired into rush hour traffic. The victims seemed randomly selected, but the motive appeared to be political, targeting employees of the Central Intelligence Agency.
Some crooked cops in the Big Easy break the laws they were sworn to uphold.
In the 1970's and 80s, people went to Alaska looking for a fresh start, to reinvent themselves, or to disappear for a while. Some of those disappearances weren't by choice.
Two brothers abduct and murder bank president Dan Short.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: The Coffee Shop Murders
programmes.d: At a coffee shop in Washington, DC, three employees were shot to death. Evidence at the crime scene pointed in many different directions. Was this a hate crime, a robbery gone wrong or an act of cold-blooded vengeance?
In 1984, a couple swept through six states like a plague, acting without rhyme or reason.

In a city awash in narcotics the drug lords have all the power even over the police. Corruption in New Orleans grew like cancer, eating away at public safety and threatening to destroy the city. Crooked cops break the laws they were sworn to uphold.
In December 1994, Joann Katrinak and her 4-month-old son mysteriously disappeared.

Willow Springs, Illinois, seemed like any other quiet Midwestern community. But it was really one of the most corrupt places in the nation. This tiny village, nestled just outside of Chicago, was in the hip pocket of organized crime.
The FBI began an undercover operation to expose the Chicago Mafia's infiltration.

Power is a responsibility as well as a privilege. But in the wrong hands, power can corrupt. For former Deputy Attorney General for the State of Delaware, losing sight of his sworn oath to uphold justice could prove lethal.
FBI agents' attempt to apprehend two murder suspects leads to a bloody firefight.

In the 1980's, two partners created a nightclub that would bring them wealth and international fame. The male strip club phenomenon promised female patrons fun and excitement. But the bright lights hid a dark side.
The bodies of several women began turning up around the city of Vienna, Austria.
In June of 1997, a crime wave swept Iowa like a tornado. It left a trail of robbery, kidnapping, and murder in its wake, and then it moved on. No one knew where.
A sniper murdered two young Black men as they jogged with two white women.

A businessman went to Florida to make one last deal before he retired-he never returned home to his millions. Authorities examined who was closest to him and who stood to gain from his disappearance. But this time conventional rules didn't apply.
The FBI searches for a man who sneaks up on police officers in patrol cars and opens fire.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Cat and Mouse
programmes.d: He was a predator, abducting girls and young women from their own front yards in broad daylight. He was a sadist: phoning one victim's family, taunting them, boosting then dashing their hope, and he wouldn't stop until we stopped him.
Six Black males had been brutally murdered; two had their hearts cut out.

Drops of blood and a torn screen were all that's left to tell authorities what happened to a woman in Indiana. The 21 yr. old victim was taken from her home on a spring morning. She appeared to have no real enemies, there was no clear motive.
In 1990, a 14-year-old girl ran away from her Texas home and disappeared.

The disappearance of young women triggered a search that spanned the Pacific Northwest. A massive media campaign failed to locate the drifter, who first charmed then killed them. As investigators followed his trail, he always stayed one step ahead.
When a woman vanishes, police suspect that her former lover is responsible.

In Miami, a gang of robbers targeted banks and armored cars. They carried assault weapons and weren't afraid to use them. They struck during the day, and sometimes twice a day. For awhile, they seemed unstoppable.
Powerful street gangs in Washington D.C. enforced their power with deadly violence.

When a sniper in Utah started targeting African-American men for death, authorities launched a massive investigation. With scant clues and no witnesses they found the odds stacked against them, and they had no idea where the killer would strike next.
Masked bandits pulled off a daring bank robbery in the middle of the day.
Two young boys were the only witnesses to their mother's murder. The horrible crime appeared unmotivated, senseless and random.
Authorities in a small Washington town began investigating the disappearance of a young woman.
Bank robbery is a brazen yet simple crime. A mask, a gun, a note passed to a teller. But bank burglary is different. It takes skill to disable an alarm, to penetrate a locked vault.
A stranger snatched an eight-year-old girl as she played in her Tucson, Arizona neighborhood.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Death In The Delta
programmes.d: When a wealthy young woman was abducted in front of her in-laws' home, the police had no shortage of suspects. The 25-year-old victim left behind a tumultuous marriage, an ex-husband and old boyfriends. All were on the FBI's short list.
In 1989, Marine Captain Shirley Russell failed to report for duty at the base in Quantico, Virginia.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Driven to Kill
programmes.d: A serial rapist targeted women. His dark urges raged out of control and led him to murder. He followed a path so random it was impossible to trace, and all that tied him to his crimes were his access to the highways and a bizarre sexual fetish.
New Jersey millionaire Frank Black flew to West Palm Beach, Florida to close a major business deal.

A killer was on the loose in one of America's most popular tourist destinations. Armed and desperate, he evaded law enforcement at every turn. As the Fourth of July weekend quickly approached, thousands of people became potential targets.
In 1997, the FBI and the NYPD began a joint investigation into Gurmeet Dhinsa for gas pump rigging.

A burning body in a dark alley shed light on a cold-blooded killer. His partners in crime would tell the story, if they lived. In the underworld of the drug trade, even a childhood friend can quickly become an enemy.
Police question a notorious cult after finding the decapitated body of a black man.

Agents follow a bounty hunter and a former police officer after the theft of an armored van.
